{"summary":"The design specifies an idempotent webhook receiver as a set of conceptual components: an ingress endpoint that accepts inbound webhook calls, an idempotency check that consults a dedupe store before any processing occurs, a processing handler that performs the business action exactly once per unique event, and a response component that acknowledges the sender. The design intentionally stays abstract about the storage technology and sender identity because the input does not specify them.","data_flow_description":"An inbound HTTP request arrives at the Webhook Ingress Endpoint carrying an event payload and (assumed) some form of unique identifier. The endpoint extracts this identifier and passes it to the Idempotency Check, which queries the Dedupe Store to determine whether the event has already been processed. If the event is new, the Processing Handler executes the business logic and the Dedupe Store is updated to mark the event processed; the flow then proceeds to the Response Sender, which returns an acknowledgement to the caller. If the event is a duplicate, the Idempotency Check short-circuits the flow directly to the Response Sender, which still returns a success acknowledgement without re-invoking the Processing Handler, so a retried delivery produces no additional side effects.","components": [],"unknown_disposition": [],"trade_offs":[],"rejected_approaches":[],"automation_verdict":{"warranted":true,"statement":"placeholder"}}
